newsitem.title: USA: Cephalon,Chiron fall on FDA action.
newsitem.headline: Cephalon,Chiron fall on FDA action.

text.p: Shares of Cephalon Inc fell sharply Friday and Chiron Corp's stock also retreated following a Food and Drug Administration panel vote to reject the companies' Myotrophin drug for Lou Gehrig's Disease.
While Chiron and Cephalon were to have split profits from the drug, analysts said the FDA vote is much more of a blow to Cephalon, which is a development-stage company with no drugs on the market.
Cepthalon shares were down 7-5/8 to 12-3/8 and Chiron dropped 1-1/8 to 18-7/8.

Analysts said that while the FDA vote was not entirely a surprise, many observers had also seen a chance the panel would clear the drug for approval because of some successful trial results and because of the severity of the disease.
Lou Gehrig's Disease, which is officially known as amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, is a crippling nervous system disorder that kills about 10,000 people in the U.S. each year.

One pivotal trial of Myotrophin showed clear statistical significance, but results of a second were debated and an FDA panel last year suggested the companies conduct a third. They failed to do so, however.
Bear Stearns analyst Ethan Lovell, however, said he thought a seven or eight point drop in Cephalon was overdone, considering that the sales potential for Myotrophin was limited.

"There are 30,000 or 35,000 ALS patients in the U.S. and not all of them would have benefited from the drug. And Cephalon would have had to split its profits with Chiron," Lovell said. He said in his view with FDA vote was worth a drop of about $5 in Cephalon's stock and $1 or $2 in Chiron's.

Analysts also noted that the drug could still be a viable candidate for approval if the companies conducted a third trial. But they said they considered it doubtful Cephalon and Chiron would be willing to invest the time and money to do so. -Andrea Orr 213 380-2014
